title: Arranger and pianist Jay Golson and later pianists
summary: Jay Golson, a piano player and still a great arranger, wrote much of the book; Lionel Reason was a later pianist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: He never got the plan that the rest of his family did, huh?
Jay Golson didn't have anybody in the family. Wasn't he related to Benny the Tenno player?
How do you spell his name?
G-H-O-L-S-O-N. He's the only one in the family.
Oh, well I must have the family.
He's still a great arranger. He's still a great arranger. He arranges from Motown. He was a piano player that really wrote the part of my book. It was great, great arrangements. Mm-hmm.
Was he came in after Lloyd then?
Right. No, I, yes he did, after Lloyd. See, Lloyd didn't stay a long, long time. Jay Golson came in. And then from here when I reorganized the band was Lionel Reason. Mm-hmm. That was the pianist.
